This is the snippet from the issue body: a StructuredBuffer of a struct holding a
single 4x4 matrix of 16-bit floats, reading two elements of the first row and two
of the last.

In the DXC panes, look at the RawBufferLoad calls near the bottom of the output.
Their fourth operand is a byte offset into the buffer element. Compare those four
offsets against the element size printed in the "Buffer Definitions" comment block
at the top of the same pane, and against the alignment operand the same calls
carry: the loads step by twice the size of the scalar type they are loading, so
the last two read past the end of the element entirely.

Compiler Explorer runs Release builds and appends debug-info flags to DXC panes,
neither of which affects this: the compile succeeds and the wrong offsets are in
the emitted DXIL.
